## Market Availability Checks for MOVE

Before depositing funds, verify current MOVE market availability directly in the exchange or DEX interface. Listings, liquidity, regional access, and withdrawal networks change over time, so treat venue availability as something to confirm at the point of purchase.

Use this checklist before placing an order:
- Search for the exact MOVE ticker and Movement name.
- Confirm the trading pair, contract address, and network.
- Compare spread, volume, withdrawal fees, and minimum order size.
- Send a small test withdrawal before moving a larger balance.

## Step by Step Verification

First, confirm the trading pair and quote currency. Second, compare spread, 24h volume, and minimum order size. Third, verify the withdrawal network and any contract address shown by the venue. Fourth, review fees before funding the account. Fifth, send a small test withdrawal before moving a larger balance to self-custody.

## Custody and Transfer Planning

Before purchasing MOVE, decide whether the position will remain on a venue temporarily or move to a wallet. Confirm that the wallet supports the correct network. If the token exists on multiple chains, select the chain carefully, because sending assets over the wrong network can permanently lose funds.

## Fees, Slippage, and Order Type

Fees are not limited to the visible trading fee. Users should also compare spread, deposit fees, withdrawal fees, card or bank fees, minimum order size, and network fees. Limit orders can reduce execution uncertainty compared with market orders, but they may not fill. For decentralized venues, slippage settings and pool liquidity are critical checks.

## Records and Taxes

Keep records of the date, amount, price, fees, transaction IDs, and transfer destination. Tax treatment varies by jurisdiction, and TokenRadar does not provide tax advice. Good records make it easier to reconcile cost basis, transfers, and realized gains or losses later.

## FAQ

**Where can I buy Movement?**

TokenRadar does not assert live venue availability in generated articles. Check current MOVE support directly inside the venue or DEX interface you are eligible to use.

**What should I verify before buying MOVE?**

Verify ticker, token name, contract or network, liquidity, spread, fees, withdrawal status, and regional eligibility before funding an account.

**Is Movement safe to buy?**

No article can make that determination. Current market data, TokenRadar risk score, liquidity, supply, custody setup, and personal risk tolerance all matter.

**Should I move MOVE to a wallet?**

That depends on custody preference and network support. If you self-custody, use a small test transfer and confirm the receiving network before moving a larger amount.

## Continue Research

After checking where MOVE can be traded, compare the Movement overview with the [price scenario page](/movement/price-prediction). The overview keeps risk score, market [cap](/cap-4), volume, and supply context together, while the scenario page separates upside, base, and downside conditions. If you plan to self-custody, review the [hardware wallet guide](/best-crypto-hardware-wallets) before moving funds and keep the [tax workflow guide](/crypto-tax-guide) open while recording fills, fees, withdrawals, and transfer IDs.

For MOVE research, the important control is consistency between the live market snapshot and the longer historical record. A single 24h move can be noisy, while market [cap](/cap-4) rank, 30-day performance, all-time high distance, supply structure, and volume-to-cap ratio create a more durable comparison set. This is why the article separates market data from decision rules and keeps the conclusion conditional.

Movement also needs category-aware interpretation. A Infrastructure token with high liquidity can behave very differently from a low-volume asset with the same percentage move. The practical question is whether volume, spread quality, supply data, and catalyst evidence confirm the move or contradict it.

The safest way to use this how to-buy article is as a checklist. Confirm the latest price, check the current rank, compare 24h volume with market cap, review the ATH and ATL dates, and look for any project-specific changes before treating the data as current enough for research.
